statement: Hand-frozen cohort definition for the Task 4 measurement baseline. The collector resolves this spec into tools/ci-measurement/dataset-2026-09.json exactly once; `resolved_run_ids` is filled in from that collection so a --refetch reproducibility check can replay the identical run list. Nothing here authorizes a workflow, ruleset, or cadence change.

fingerprint.definition: Comparability is job STRUCTURE, not workflow bytes. For a run's head SHA the workflow file is fetched with GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.github/workflows/<file>?ref=<sha>, written to a throwaway root holding only that file, composed by bin/generate-ci-workflow-inventory --root=<temp>, and reduced to a SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of every job's key, expansion, literal matrix resolution/axes/raw expression, sorted needs, aggregate gate token, and sorted visible contexts. A run is comparable when that hash equals the hash of the checked-out workflow.
fingerprint.excluded: Everything a reformat, a comment, a runner-image bump, a step edit, a timeout, or a permissions change would alter. The fingerprint bounds the job graph and nothing else.
fingerprint.cache_key: the workflow file's git blob SHA, so N distinct blobs cost N generator runs

pull_request.rationale: The primary cohort. Walked newest-first until at least 60 comparable completed runs contain at least 15 with conclusion `failure`. Cancelled runs are skipped because a superseded-run cancellation is not a defect; `action_required` runs never executed. Every skipped run is recorded with its reason.

main_push.rationale: Post-merge comparator: the 20 most recent completed push-on-main runs with a matching fingerprint.

nightly.rationale: Scheduled comparator: EVERY completed nightly.yml run. This cohort is `exhaustive` — "all of them", not "at least N" — so the walk never stops early and is complete only when the run listing itself ran out, never when the page budget did. `target_runs` is therefore a floor of one, not a count: hard-coding the number of nightly runs that happen to exist would put a volatile count into a governance artifact. nightly.yml is a different workflow from ci.yml, so its fingerprint is computed over nightly.yml and RECORDED for auditability rather than used as a filter.

collection.attempts: every attempt of every kept run, via GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs?filter=all&per_page=100
collection.pull_request_resolution: run.pull_requests[] when present; otherwise GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls, because run.pull_requests[] empties once the pull request is merged or closed. Which path answered is recorded as `pr_source`.
collection.artifacts: GET /actions/runs/{id}/artifacts?per_page=100, recorded as evidence state with each artifact's expiry flag
collection.freeze: The dataset commits the exact run ids, attempt numbers, head SHAs, PR numbers, workflow blob SHAs, the fingerprint, the query parameters and a collected_at timestamp. Jobs and steps of a completed run do not change, so a re-collection of the committed run-id list reproduces the observed fields byte for byte; anything time-dependent (log availability, artifact expiry) is recorded as evidence state rather than silently absent.
collection.cohort_shapes: Two cohort shapes. An ordinary cohort walks newest-first and stops as soon as its floor (`target_runs` and `target_failures`) is met. An `exhaustive` cohort never stops early: it consumes the whole listing, and its `target_met` is true only when the LISTING ended the walk (`listing_exhausted`) and the floor holds, so a cohort truncated by `max_pages` can never read as complete.

unavailable.billed_runner_minutes: Structurally unavailable. On a public repository GET /actions/runs/{id}/timing reports duration_ms 0 per job, and organization billing requires an admin:org scope this tooling does not hold. Summed job-wall seconds weighted by GitHub's published per-OS runner multipliers (ubuntu 1, windows 2, macos 10) is recorded as a COST PROXY and labelled as one.
